title: Private agent upgrade caused tight-retry loop → ephemeral port exhaustion & control-plane connectivity degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of private-orchestrator-2.4.0 to customer VPCs, a change in the agent TLS handshake/backoff behavior caused a subset of upgraded agents to enter a tight-retry loop when presented with transient certificate validation failures. The retry storm caused per-host ephemeral port exhaustion on NAT gateways and CPU pressure on the orchestrator control-plane proxies, which led to intermittent control-plane disconnects and degraded API responsiveness for affected customers. Impact window: 2026-02-27T02:15Z — 2026-02-27T05:40Z. Root cause: regression in agent retry/backoff logic combined with insufficient client-side circuit-breaking and missing observable metrics around ephemeral port usage and TLS handshake failure rates.
updates: 2026-02-27: Incident detected by ops on-call via elevated control-plane latency alerts and thousands of failed agent TLS handshakes in logs (dashboards link: https://dash.internal/redwood/incidents/52910).
2026-02-27: Rolled partial rollback of 2.4.0 to canary ring; engineering paused further rollouts and opened this follow-up ticket.
2026-02-27: Identified tight-retry loop in new agent client — missing exponential backoff/jitter when TLS validation fails; reproduced locally with expired cert fixture.

2026-02-28: Mitigation steps applied: introduced short-term on-agent rate limiting (config flag) and emergency config to increase ephemeral port range on affected NAT gateways where possible; ops verified reduction in retry volume.

2026-03-01: Hotfix PR created to reintroduce exponential backoff with jitter + per-agent circuit breaker (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/412), awaiting review from runtime team.
2026-03-03: Added temporary control-plane-side throttle to drop excessive reconnect attempts per source IP; this reduced CPU pressure while we validated the agent hotfix.
2026-03-05: Assignee updated to Marco Rivera to lead action item implementation and cross-team coordination with networking and customer success teams.
acceptance_criteria: Agent hotfix merged and released (private-agent >= 2.4.1) that restores exponential backoff with jitter and enforces a per-agent circuit breaker with a tracked state metric.
Control plane implements source-IP-based soft-throttling and emits metrics for dropped/rejected reconnect attempts.
Ephemeral port utilization dashboards created and alerted on (thresholds defined: 75%, 90%).
Runbook updated and validated for private upgrade scenarios to include preflight certificate checks and staged canary gating based on TLS handshake success rates.
Customer-facing postmortem draft completed and shared with impacted customers via Customer Success.
action_items: AI-1: Ship agent hotfix (private-agent PR#412) — reintroduce exponential backoff + jitter; add config-driven circuit-breaker (owner: Marco Rivera; estimate: 3 points; due: 2026-03-08).
AI-2: Add metrics: agent.tls_handshake_failures, agent.retry_state_changes, agent.circuit_breaker_trips (owner: Runtime Observability; estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-10).
AI-3: Create ephemeral port utilization dashboard and alerts for private customers and internal NATs (owner: Network Reliability; estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-09).

AI-4: Update private upgrade runbook with TLS preflight step and gating rules based on handshake success rate; include rollback playbook for tight-retry signatures (owner: PM - Ryan Cho; estimate: 1; due: 2026-03-05).
AI-5: Implement control-plane soft-throttling policy for excessive reconnects by source IP and circuit-breaker eviction metrics (owner: Control Plane; estimate: 3; due: 2026-03-12).
AI-6: Postmortem write-up and customer communication draft (owner: Customer Success; estimate: 1; due: 2026-03-06).
AI-7: Run a chaos test in staging that simulates broken certs during rolling upgrade to validate backoff & throttling behavior (owner: SRE; estimate: 2; due: 2026-03-15).
